original_value: With the development of Internet of Things (IoT) applications, applying the potential and benefits of IoT technology in the health and environment services is increasing to improve the service quality using sensors and devices. This paper aims to apply GIS-based optimization algorithms for optimizing IoT-based network deployment through the use of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and smart connected sensors for environmental and health applications. First, the WSN deployment research studies in health and environment applications are reviewed including fire monitoring, precise agriculture, telemonitoring, smart home, and hospital. Second, the WSN deployment process is modeled to optimize two conflict objectives, coverage and lifetime, by applying Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) routing protocol with minimum total network lengths. Third, the performance of the Bees Algorithm (BA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithms are compared for the evaluation of GIS-based WSN deployment in health and environment applications. The algorithms were compared using convergence rate, constancy repeatability, and modeling complexity criteria. The results showed that the PSO algorithm converged to higher values of objective functions gradually while BA found better fitness values and was faster in the first iterations. The levels of stability and repeatability were high with 0.0150 of standard deviation for PSO and 0.0375 for BA. The PSO also had lower complexity than BA. Therefore, the PSO algorithm obtained better performance for IoT-based sensor network deployment.

result.paraphrase: As Internet of Things (IoT) applications expand, IoT’s potential and benefits in health and environmental services are increasingly being used to improve service quality through sensors and devices. This paper proposes GIS-based optimization algorithms for optimizing IoT network deployment via wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and smart connected sensors in environmental and health applications. It first reviews WSN deployment studies in health and environmental uses, including fire monitoring, precision agriculture, telemonitoring, smart homes, and hospitals. Next, the WSN deployment process is modeled to optimize two conflicting objectives, coverage and lifetime, using the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) routing protocol with minimum total network length. Finally, the Bees Algorithm (BA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are compared to evaluate GIS-based WSN deployment in health and environmental applications. The comparison uses convergence rate, stability repeatability, and modeling complexity. Results showed that PSO gradually converged to higher objective-function values, while BA found better fitness values and was faster in the initial iterations. Stability and repeatability were high, with standard deviations of 0.0150 for PSO and 0.0375 for BA. PSO also had lower complexity than BA. Therefore, PSO performed better for IoT-based sensor network deployment.
